guide.summary: The request fits Notion's OAuth 2.0 integration flow, which is documented for apps that act on behalf of each user. Because customers in other organizations/workspaces will connect, the integration must be a public integration rather than one limited to selected workspaces. Authorization can start once client credentials and a redirect URI are configured, and Marketplace review is not required for authorization. The 'Read content' capability covers reading page titles and content, and each customer must share pages through the page picker. The sources do not document a customer-admin approval step for public installs, so that remains unknown.

details.title: Use the OAuth 2.0 authorization flow with a public integration
details.detail: OAuth integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol. Users are sent to the authorization URL, Notion redirects with a temporary code, and the app exchanges the code at the token endpoint for an access token used on each user's behalf.
details.appliesWhen: Each customer connects its own Notion account or workspace to the app.

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: Read content: Read content is the only capability needed to read page titles and content shared through OAuth. The markdown endpoint requires Read content and returns 403 without it. Access is limited to pages the user shares through the page picker, and page children are included if the parent is shared. No create, update or admin capability is requested.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register a public OAuth integration with Read content only
In the Developer portal, open Build > Connections and create a new connection. Choose Any workspace (public integration), since other customer workspaces will connect, and enable only the Read content capability. Installation scope cannot be changed later. This step does not authorize any customer.
Fields: Installation scope: Any workspace (public), not selected workspaces, Capability: Read content only; no insert or update

Record OAuth client ID, client secret and redirect URI
Open the Configuration tab of the connection to read the OAuth client ID and client secret. Register the exact redirect URI and keep the secret out of source control, for example in an environment variable. Use the same redirect URI in the authorization URL and token request.
Fields: CLIENT_ID: Configuration tab, OAuth client ID, CLIENT_SECRET: Configuration tab, OAuth client secret, REDIRECT_URI: must exactly match the registered redirect URI

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Authorize the app as a customer and select shared pages in the page picker
Done when: The redirect contains a code query parameter, and the customer's selected pages are the only pages the test may read.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The response is HTTP 200 with a JSON access_token, refresh_token and workspace_id, and the token is stored for the authorized customer.

Retrieve a customer-shared page and read its title
Done when: HTTP 200 returns object page with the page id and a title value read from the properties title entry. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Read the content of the same shared page as Markdown
Done when: HTTP 200 returns a markdown field containing the page content, and any truncated or unknown block state is recorded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Confirm a page not selected by the customer is not readable
Done when: The request returns HTTP 404 with object_not_found for the unselected page, and the grant selection is recorded.
